children: Wheat fell towards $7.12 per bushel, the lowest level in three weeks, as renewed hopes for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire raised expectations of reduced disruption to Black Sea grain shipments.
US President Donald Trump announced a truce on strikes on Russia and Ukraine's energy facilities.
Also, Turkey is seeking to broker a broader agreement between Kyiv and Moscow that could stop attacks on ships in the Black Sea.
Ukraine has indicated it would support such a deal if Russia agrees, while the Kremlin has described the proposal positively.
The prospect of improved trade flows has added pressure to wheat prices, which remain below the 3½-year high of $7.67 reached on August 28.
Meanwhile, the latest USDA forecasts pointed to slightly above-average global wheat inventories.
The agency also lowered its 2026/27 export forecasts for Russia by 3 million metric tons to 43 million tons and for Ukraine by 1 million tons to 12.5 million tons

title: Wheat Falls to 3-Week Low
